summary: Independent whole-branch review found two important failure-path gaps: CI skipped coverage after earlier failures, and Vitest suppressed reports from failed coverage suites.

decisions.ruling: Remediate both failure-path gaps before completion.
decisions.reason: An artifact uploaded with no generated reports is not useful failure evidence, and failures are precisely when coverage data is most valuable.
decisions.costIfWrong: Coverage now deliberately runs after prior validation failures when dependency installation completed, which can add diagnostic time to a failed CI job.

summary: Verified that CI permits coverage after earlier non-cancellation failures once dependencies install, and that an intentionally failing covered suite preserves its coverage reports while keeping a nonzero exit status.
command: failure-path configuration assertion; temporary failing domain coverage probe; pnpm coverage; pnpm lint; pnpm typecheck; pnpm test; pnpm e2e; pnpm test:impacted -- --dry-run
evidence: Before the fix, the failure-path configuration assertion failed and the temporary failed domain suite produced no coverage summary.
After the fix, the same domain suite exited 1 and preserved HTML, LCOV, and JSON summary reports (368/415 covered lines).
After probe removal, pnpm coverage restored normal reports; lint, typecheck, five Vitest targets, Chromium E2E, and impact preview all passed.
Normal coverage output excludes the temporary probe and still reports apps/crm-web/src/app/app.tsx as uncovered.

summary: Independent read-only re-review of the remediation found no remaining critical, important, or minor issues and confirmed that failure and cancellation semantics remain intact.
evidence: Re-review range 891d28b..f69acb2.
Coverage runs after ordinary upstream failures only when dependency installation succeeded and the workflow was not cancelled.
All three coverage targets preserve reports on failing suites without continue-on-error or lost pipe failure status.

decisions.ruling: Accept the failure-path remediation without adding a global report merger, thresholds, or browser-code coverage.
decisions.reason: Those behaviors were explicitly out of scope and are not needed to make the baseline reports dependable.
decisions.costIfWrong: Future coverage policy remains a separate reviewed change.

summary: Designed Policy, Policy State, Finance, and service-bus boundaries for the reference CRM, with typed events and durable regression evidence as the portable-agent contract.
evidence: User requirement: Policy and Policy State communicate through events; Finance consumes state/events.
Existing Test API is a deterministic in-memory adapter and will compose the new runtime rather than call the shared reducer directly.

decisions.ruling: Use a typed in-process FIFO service bus and library service boundaries rather than a production broker.
decisions.reason: It exercises event ownership, delivery, idempotency, and failure semantics without external credentials, timing races, or CI cost.
decisions.costIfWrong: A real transport can implement the same message contracts later; it is intentionally outside this reference harness.

summary: First design review identified missing enforceable service ownership, delivery/retry semantics, separate command/message identity, concrete Policy State projection, exact rule evidence, and implementable coverage/record gates; the design and plan were revised before implementation.
evidence: Review round 1: service stores must be private; Finance initializes only from policy.state.changed.
Delivery now specifies FIFO, subscriber order, pending retry, receipt-after-success, and failure log behavior.
Rule evidence now requires exact Vitest and Playwright test identities, not file-level tags.

decisions.ruling: Separate commandId, messageId, correlationId, and causationId and carry tenant/schema/timestamp on every envelope.
decisions.reason: One overloaded source-event ID could not prove client idempotency, message de-duplication, or causal event chains.
decisions.costIfWrong: The API and fixtures need deterministic ID/clock ports, increasing the initial reference-runtime surface.

summary: Created a seven-task TDD plan for the service bus, Policy, Policy State, Finance, composed runtime/Test API, visible CRM evidence, and enforceable rule/coverage/record safeguards.

decisions.ruling: A failed consumer leaves its envelope at the queue head and stops later consumers until a subsequent drain retries it.
decisions.reason: This makes partial delivery visible and keeps recovery deterministic without silently continuing downstream effects.
